content: This medication, ampicillin, is a penicillin-type antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is not effective against viral infections such as the common cold or flu. It should be taken by mouth as directed by your doctor, typically four times a day (every six hours). For optimal absorption, take it on an empty stomach, either one hour before or two hours after a meal, with a full glass of water. To ensure the best results, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals and continue the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or sores in the mouth or on the tongue. These effects are usually mild and temporary. However, this medication may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition known as Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea, which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use of ampicillin may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Ampicillin can commonly cause a mild rash, which is usually not serious. However, it is important to distinguish this from a rare rash that may indicate a severe allergic reaction. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but may include symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. Seek immediate medical attention if these occur. Before taking ampicillin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other penicillin antibiotics, or cephalosporins, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Ampicillin may also reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, as it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Ampicillin may interfere with certain lab tests, such as some diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false results. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. In case of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for more details on how to safely discard it. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
